claim: F_q[T], exact integers, q = 7 and 13, N = 2 and 3, long marks (lam > N, lam > d), 58 configurations, rules fixed before the runs. The row is a sum of blocks over the marked primes, each block the unmarked row twisted by a cubic character (model form of Lemmas S1, S2); identity E = D + (SD - D) + CRperp + CRcoh checked against an explicit double sum over pairs of primes (6 small configurations, 8 vectors). The slot-diagonal part equals the diagonal up to O(N q^(N - lam/2)) (proved, Weil; measured within 2.4e-3 for lam >= 7), so the model excess (target a: 20.64 at q = 7 (2,12,1); 2.34 at q = 13 (2,7,2)) is the cross term over pairs of distinct marked primes; random signs on the marked primes return the vector to the diagonal. The exact squared signal B on the Gauss-sum rows is carried by pairs of primes; Cross = B + (n - 1) D, n <= 1.5 in 593 of 596 vector-configurations; the registered rule fails at (2,12,1) for the second target (n = 5.31; B/D = 2.16 of e = 7.47), one random-multiplicative seed and the Liouville-twisted vector at (2,11,2). Post hoc: the remainder is a second squared signal in the direction u(m); the trivial target is unresolved at d = 3. Completed rows N = 3: the cube-term excess is cross and lies in the span enlarged by V c_0, V c_1. Model against the Z[omega] screen: no disagreement; at short marks (lam = N/3, N/4) the model has no target excess (ratio 0.975 to 0.997) and the Liouville-twisted vector +3.4 to +8.7 in the cross term; in Z[omega] the class sums of the THETA dual vector are at the random-phase level and the predicted coherent cross is 1.5e-4 to 3.2e-4 of the diagonal (resolution 0.01 to 0.02); visibility needs about 1e10 columns or more with P >= Z^2 (argued). Removes the caveat of round-9 lesson 1; no flag.
